_readme: HUMAN-AUTHORED FILE. CI NEVER WRITES BACK (ADR-0042 D6). The update protocol — what a re-baseline PR must state — lives in baseline.README.md next to this file. Read it before changing a number here.
_what_these_numbers_are: Hosted-runner (ubuntu-latest) means, in NANOSECONDS, with a per-benchmark tolerance band in PERCENT. They are deliberately NOT the workstation figures published in README.md / docs/README-technical.md (AMD Ryzen 9 9900X, 12C/24T), which are 1.97x-2.35x faster; gating against those would red this job permanently (ADR-0042 D4, Option D). Regression protection is this file's job; document-vs-record correspondence is COHERENCE's (D7). The two are separate failures and are detected separately.
_dispatch_1_observer_note: ObserverDispatchBenchmark.Dispatch_1Observer is measured but deliberately NOT banded: it is declared in `unbanded`, so its presence and its measurement are checked and its value is not banded (a mean of 0 is a measurement at the floor, not a missing one). Its mean sits at BenchmarkDotNet's resolution floor: on 2026-09-20 it read 0.2145 ns with a StdDev of 1.6012 ns - seven times the mean - and BenchmarkDotNet raised ZeroMeasurement, "the method duration is indistinguishable from the empty method duration". A percentage band around a figure that small tracks the harness, not the code: it produced the two largest breaches in issue #275 (+77.19% and +66.49% FASTER) on runs where nothing in this repository changed. The published ~0.21 ns/observer figure (README.md) is unaffected - it is COHERENCE against Tests/Verbara.Sdk.Benchmarks/performance-record.json (ADR-0042 D7) - and dispatch cost stays gated by Dispatch_10Observers and Dispatch_100Observers. Restore a band only if the benchmark is rewritten to measure a workload above the floor.
_channel_manager_one_subscriber_note: ChannelManagerBenchmark.Update1000ChannelStates_OneSubscriber is baselined on BYTES only (208,000 B per thousand observed changes, exact). It is the same thousand state changes as Update1000ChannelStates on a table with one subscribed handler - the shape of every production host - added because the unsubscribed row cannot see what an observed change costs. Its time has no hosted-runner observations, and a band guessed from a workstation would not match the runner (Update1000ChannelStates reads about 66 us on ubuntu-latest and about 35 us on the workstation), so its mean_ns/tolerance_pct are set from two weekly runs, in their own PR.
_create_1000_channels_note: ChannelManagerBenchmark.Create1000Channels mean_ns moved 353,056 -> 434,153 ns (x1.2297, +22.97%, slower) when PERF_GATE_ENFORCE was turned on, for an accepted cost: the per-linkedid call index of #533, which every channel creation now maintains, so a call is found on its own server. That cost was measured against v2.9.0 on one host, interleaved, both arms under the ISA pin: the counted ABAB read 1.2442 and 1.2152 (mean of ratios 1.2297), a third round 1.1934; its bytes are not re-read here: `bytes` was already re-read on the hosted runner after #533, and the hosted run of 2026-11-13 matched it to the byte. The factor is the counted mean, applied to the pre-#533 hosted calibration, not a new calibration: the band stayed 30% then (it is 40% since, see _channel_manager_widened_bands_note), and the hosted runs of 2026-11-11 (561,348 ns, +59.0% against the old figure, +29.3% against this one) and 2026-11-13 (faster) are fleet spread, not code. Update1000ChannelStates did not move: the same ABAB read it at 1.0281 against v2.9.0, inside its bar, with no accepted cost, so its 65,925 ns stays.
_channel_manager_widened_bands_note: WIDENED BANDS. ChannelManagerBenchmark.Update1000ChannelStates went 15% -> 35% and Create1000Channels 30% -> 40%, mean_ns unchanged on both, because the runner fleet, not the code, put them at or past their SLOWER edge once the gate enforced. The hosted run of 2026-11-11 (EPYC 7763, x86-64-v3) read Update at 83,332 ns, +26.4% against 65,925 (a breach), and Create at 561,348 ns, +29.3% against 434,153 (0.7 points of margin), while every other gated row on that run read within about 6% of the four earlier EPYC 7763 runs (2026-09-20 to 10-18, Update 68,253-69,469 ns). That is not the code: an interleaved run on one workstation, JIT at x86-64-v3 and DOTNET_PROCESSOR_COUNT=4, of the 2026-10-18 commit (R0), v2.9.0 (R1) and main (H) in the order R0 R1 H H R1 R0 read Update at H/R0 = 1.007 and 1.025 (R1/R0 1.014 and 1.039), with the prediction (H/R0 <= 1.08 in both rounds) and the flip rule (>= 1.15 in both) written before the run; Create read H/R0 1.310 and 1.285: the #533 cost accepted above (1.2297 when it was measured), within H's own 13-20 us standard deviation on this run, so its mean_ns is not re-derived here. Post-pin the fleet is four CPU models (EPYC 9V45, 9V74, 7763, Xeon 6975P-C) across 7 runs, Update reading 42-55 us on three of them and 83 us on the 7763 once, so a re-pooled mean would lower the centre and deepen the 7763 red; the bands moved instead. 35% puts Update's bar at 89,000 ns, 8.6 points over the worst read; 40% puts Create's at 607,814 ns, 10.7 points over it. The cost: on an EPYC 7763 the SLOWER bar moves from about +9% to about +29% over its usual Update reading, and on the three faster models it was already +38% to +80% over theirs, so a 10-20% time regression on these rows is not seen by a band on any host. Their bytes stay exact (32,000 B and 1,054,656 B) and still fail an allocation regression. These two bands held only until the weekly job compared a reference build and this one in the same job, on the same host. Since 2026-11-19 that comparison enforces and judges both rows on time, so they keep this width and stop being provisional (baseline.README.md, the third series' result); they become provisional again if PERF_ABAB_ENFORCE goes back to 'false' or either row gets judge_time false.
_bytes_note: BYTES DECIDE, TIME INFORMS. `bytes` is BenchmarkDotNet's Memory.BytesAllocatedPerOperation and `bytes_tolerance` an absolute two-sided bound in bytes (0 = exact). Allocated bytes do not depend on the CPU model or its vector width: two local runs on .NET 10.0.14, one with the JIT at x86-64-v3 and one at x86-64-v4, gave identical bytes on every row below, while an interleaved run moved time by at most about 5% on that host; the spread across hosted runners is what a re-calibration under the ISA pin measures. They DO depend on the logical core count wherever the code sizes a structure by it (a ConcurrentDictionary built without a concurrency level), so every `bytes` here is the hosted runner's 4-core figure: read from a hosted run, or locally under DOTNET_PROCESSOR_COUNT=4, which reproduces it to the byte (checked on two commits of hosted runs, 872,024 B and 1,046,656 B on Create1000Channels). Rows with `bytes` and no `mean_ns` are gated on bytes only until two weekly runs give their time band. The two AsyncEventPumpBenchmark rows carry a 1 KB bound: the per-pump fixed cost of its lock, waiter list and run log, while the 10,000 slots themselves are exact. EnqueueAndConsume1000Events is not baselined on bytes at all: it is bimodal by a writer/consumer race (about 32 KB or about 50 KB), so equality is not a bar for it.
_isa_note: `jit_isa` pins what the comparison expects the JIT to target. ubuntu-latest mixes AMD EPYC 7763 (no AVX-512, x86-64-v3) and EPYC 9V74 (AVX-512, x86-64-v4), and .NET 10 uses AVX-512 where it exists, so the same code read faster or slower by host. The workflow sets DOTNET_EnableAVX512=0 for the whole job (DOTNET_EnableAVX512F=0, the older name, is accepted and ignored by .NET 10.0.14: the JIT still reports x86-64-v4), and the comparator fails closed when a BenchmarkDotNet log names any other ISA. The time bands below were calibrated before the pin, pooled across both CPUs; a re-calibration under the pin is its own PR, from observed runs.
_environment_note: `environment` pins the exact .NET SDK and runtime this job measures with, and the logical core count it expects. The workflow reads dotnet_sdk from here and installs that SDK, alone, into an empty directory, so no newer SDK or runtime preinstalled on the runner image can be picked up by roll-forward; the comparator then fails closed when a report's HostEnvironmentInfo shows another SDK, another runtime or another core count. Why: a runtime patch can change code generation (10.0.12 is when the JIT began targeting AVX-512 on the hosts that have it), and before this pin the weekly job took whatever 10.0.x the image carried, so a time breach could be the runtime and nobody could tell. The values are the ones the last four hosted runs measured with (2026-11-11 to 11-15: SDK 10.0.404, runtime 10.0.15, 4 logical cores); the run of 2026-11-08 was on 10.0.403 / 10.0.14, so the time bands below were read across more than one runtime, which a re-calibration under this pin will settle. A newer .NET patch is not measured until a PR moves these values; that PR says so, and re-reads the rows (baseline.README.md).
_abab_note: In-job comparison (ADR-0042 addendum): after the absolute gate, the weekly job builds `abab.reference_tag` (the reference's own tree) beside HEAD and measures both in the same job, in `abab.order` (R H H R R H: three rounds, round k pairs the k-th R with the k-th H), each invocation running every case in `abab.launch_count` processes (2: run-perf-abab.sh passes --launchCount to the in-job run only, never to the absolute gate, and the comparator treats a report that does not show that launch count as structural). Time is judged by r_k = mean(H_k) / mean(R_k) and their geometric mean g: SLOWER when g exceeds slower_ratio and so do a majority of the rounds, FASTER when g and a majority are under faster_ratio, UNCONFIRMED when only one of the two holds; a single round beyond a bar with g inside is ok and counted as a lone round. A case whose mean is under min_mean_ns in a HEAD invocation is shown and not judged; one under it in the reference only is judged SLOWER-only by the same rule on mean(H_k) / max(mean(R_k), min_mean_ns) against sub_floor_slower_ratio, and never FASTER. A case whose class source or BenchmarkDotNet job differs between the arms is not compared and is reported as a finding; a class with no judged row, or a run with none, is structural. Bytes are judged by the per-round difference, in every round, against the row's `bytes_tolerance` in `benchmarks`, for rows that have a `bytes` entry. `rows` holds per-row overrides (slower_ratio, faster_ratio or judge_time false, each with a reason); `accepted` holds a cost accepted by a PR as a ratio with `relative_to` naming the reference it was measured against, and the comparator refuses an entry whose relative_to is not reference_tag, so moving the tag at a release forces its accepted entries out. ENFORCING since 2026-11-19, after five consecutive runs met the prediction written before them; the switch is PERF_ABAB_ENFORCE in .github/workflows/perf-regression.yml, independent of PERF_GATE_ENFORCE. See baseline.README.md.

Verbara.Sdk.Benchmarks.AsyncEventPumpBen.reason: Its time is bimodal inside one process (a writer/consumer race, the same one that makes its bytes bimodal; see _bytes_note), so no in-job bar on one launch per invocation is a detector for it. It was the only row to break P7 of the first A/A series. Named before the second series; its time stays reported by the absolute gate, which has no band for it either (unbanded).

calibration.method: Parsed the BenchmarkDotNet `-report-full-compressed.json` artifacts of 13 real runs of .github/workflows/perf-regression.yml — 12 scheduled (weekly cron) plus 1 workflow_dispatch. `mean_ns` is the mean of those per-run means; the band is set to cover the observed across-run spread with headroom.
calibration.why_the_bands_are_wide: ubuntu-latest alternates between two CPU models and the EPYC 9V74 is uniformly faster — up to 20.7% on some benchmarks. Bands are POOLED across both fleets: one band per benchmark, wide enough for either CPU, because the workflow cannot choose its host. Within-run CV is 0.11%-0.67%; across-run CV is 0.5%-11.2%. This is why a band is NEVER derived from `Statistics.StandardDeviation` in a report — that is the within-run figure and is roughly 20x too tight, and a gate built on it would be red most weeks for reasons that have nothing to do with this repository's code.
calibration.verification: 0 breaches across all 13 runs under these bands; tightest headroom 5.8 percentage points.
calibration.two_sided: Bands are two-sided and so is the report. The SLOWER side is the regression this gate exists to catch, and it fails an enforcing run. The FASTER side is a stale-baseline signal (ADR-0042 D6) or a benchmark whose work got optimised away — it is reported as its own kind of breach, not as good news, and files the breach issue, but it does not fail the run.

sources._comment: artifacts subdirectory (relative to --artifacts-root) -> the BenchmarkDotNet type whose report MUST be there. One row per `--filter` step in .github/workflows/perf-regression.yml. Adding a filter step obliges a row here AND its baseline entries below; a row whose results/ directory or report file is missing is a HARD failure, which is what closes the `|| true` hole (ADR-0042 D4).
sources._turn_detection_note: Present here with NO rows in "benchmarks" below, and that is deliberate rather than an oversight: its four cases are declared in `unbanded`, so their presence and their measurement are checked and their value is not banded. The step must run and produce a report — a missing results/ directory is still a hard failure, which is the point — but its band cannot be calibrated yet: every other band in this file came from 13 observed runs and this benchmark has none. The PR that flipped PERF_GATE_ENFORCE left it unbaselined; its band is set from its own observations, in its own PR. Guessing one here would break the rule this file exists to enforce, in the change that wrote it.

unbanded._comment: The benchmarks of a gated class that run WITHOUT a band, on purpose, keyed by FullName exactly as the report spells it, each with its reason. Their presence and their measurement are checked (a declared entry absent from the report, or one whose Statistics.Mean is missing or not a finite number, is a structural failure); their value is not banded. Every [Benchmark] method of a `sources` class needs a `benchmarks` entry or an entry here, which the script tests check on every pull request.
